summary: Seong-Uk Kim specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Supervised by Robert E. Buswell Jr. for doctoral studies, Kim was Cho Associate Professor in Korean Culture and Religion at Columbia University (attested 2026).

Sergey Malov was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kazan Theological Academy under Nikolai Katanov and at St. Petersburg University, later holding posts at Kazan Federal University, Saint Petersburg State University, and the National Library of Russia.

Sergey Oldenburg specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg University under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, and held posts at Saint Petersburg State University, the Russian Academy of Sciences, the State Hermitage Museum, and the Asiatic Museum, which he founded.

Serinity Young was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University in 1990 under Alex Wayman and held posts at the American Museum of Natural History and Southern Methodist University in 2000.
Sesso Oda was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Zuigan Goto from circa 1927 to 1966 and later succeeded him. His students included Soko Morinaga and Gary Snyder.

Seung-yeon Lee works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Lee completed doctoral studies under Sang-hae Lee and held posts at Sungkyunkwan University and the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties.

Seunghak Koh specializes in Buddhist studies. Koh earned an MA from Seoul National University and a PhD from UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and served as an Appointed Researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Seungsahn Haengwon was a Buddhist and religious studies teacher who studied at Dongguk University and under Kobong Sunim, whom he succeeded in 1957, as well as Keumbong and Keum'oh. He founded the Kwan Um School of Zen in 1970.
Shagun Sinha works in Indology, computational studies, and linguistics. Sinha completed a PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University under doctoral supervisor Girish Nath Jha, attested in 2022.

Shailendra Bhandare specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He has held positions at the British Museum, the Fitzwilliam Museum, the Ashmolean Museum (attested 2006–2022), and St Cross College (attested 2022).

Shaman Hatley specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD), taught at Concordia University from circa 2007 to 2015, and became chair of Asian studies at the University of Massachusetts Boston in 2015.
Shan Shan Zhao specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Zhao earned a Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn.

Shanshan Jia specializes in Indology and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Harunaga Isaacson (attested 2015) and held a post there as Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).

Shaoyong Ye works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After doctoral studies at Peking University under Qing Duan, Ye held faculty appointments at Peking University as Associate Professor (attested 2010–2016) and faculty member (attested 2026).
Sharon J. Roe is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. She completed a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under doctoral supervisor Steven D. Goodman (attested 2014).

Sharon Salzberg is a teacher in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University at Buffalo and trained under teachers including Anagarika Munindra, Satya Narayan Goenka, and Dipa Ma. She co-founded the Insight Meditation Society (1974) and Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (1989).

Shashibhusan Dasgupta was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Brojomohun College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, where he earned an MA and PhD and served as Lecturer from circa 1939 to 1964.

Shayne Clarke specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison and a PhD at UCLA under Gregory Schopen, later holding posts at McMaster University and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under spiritual teacher Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and founded Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

Sheila Jasanoff studied at Radcliffe College, the University of Bonn, Harvard University, and Harvard Law School. She held academic posts at Cornell University (circa 1978–1998) and Harvard University as professor from circa 1998.
